newsitem.title: USA: US court allows limited delay on new air standards.
newsitem.headline: US court allows limited delay on new air standards.

text.p: A federal court approved a three-week delay for the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency to issue new air quality standards, EPA officials and health advocates said Monday.

The U.S. court in Arizona extended the deadline for public comments on the proposed rule to March 12 from February 18, and extended the deadline for the EPA to issue a final rule to July 19 from June 30.
Under pressure from states, counties and cities which said they needed more time to study the controversial proposal, the EPA last week asked for a 60-day extension.
The American Lung Association, which originally sued the EPA to force it to review its clean air standards, had urged the court to reject the request.
"This is a good move," said Paul Billings, assistant director of government relations for the lung association. "We just didn't want an unreasonable delay."
EPA's proposal to tighten the standards for smog-forming ozone and tiny particles in order to protect public health could put more than 160 counties out of compliance with air quality standards.
Critics of the stricter rule fear that it will force states to impose costly new pollution controls on industry, with limited health benefits.
Judge Alfredo Marqez of the U.S. District Court for the District of Arizona said in his order that he would grant "no further extensions" for the final rule.
